Test for changes in the co-localisation of cell types between conditions

Source: R/spicy_main.R
spicy.Rd

spicy() tests, for every ordered pair of cell types from → to, whether the co-localisation of the two types differs between conditions, or is associated with survival. A pair asks whether to cells are placed near from cells more than other cells are.

Usage

spicy(
  cells,
  condition,
  subject = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  imageID = "imageID",
  cellType = "cellType",
  spatialCoords = c("x", "y"),
  r = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  method = c("cell", "image"),
  effect = c("allocation", "count"),
  k = NULL,
  combine = c("maxT", "davies", "cauchy"),
  adjustAbundance = FALSE,
  variance = c("cr2", "hartung_knapp"),
  ref = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  tableKey = NULL,
  imageInfo = NULL,
  cellWeights = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

cells

A data.frame, SingleCellExperiment or SpatialExperiment with one row (column) per cell, or (cell method) the path of a SpatialData or AnnData Zarr store (read with the Rarr package). From a store, the columns are read a block of rows at a time and the coordinates a batch of whole images at a time, so the table is never held in memory; the results are those of the same cells given as a data.frame. Column names then refer to the table's obs; imageID defaults to the table's region key and spatialCoords to its obsm array "spatial". A SpatialData object (spatialdataR) read from a store is read from that store in the same way; one built in memory is analysed from its table.

condition

The column of the image-level condition: two groups, or a survival::Surv column for a survival outcome (from a store, a column of imageInfo).

subject

The column of the patient (unit) of each image. Images of one patient are combined; if omitted, every image is its own patient.

covariates

Image- or patient-level columns to adjust for (cell method: added to the design of the excess, and the effect of each is reported as <column>_effect and <column>_p_value; survival: added to the null Cox model).

imageID, cellType, spatialCoords

Column names of the image, cell type and coordinates. For a Zarr store, spatialCoords is either two obs columns or the name of one obsm array (its first two columns).

r

Radius (or radii) of the neighbourhood, in the units of the coordinates. Cell method: one radius (default 50), or several to be combined by combine. Image method: the radii of the L function (default 20, 50 and 100).

from, to

Cell types to test (all ordered pairs by default).

method

"cell" (spicyR Cell, the default) or "image" (the original spicyR test).

effect

Cell method: "allocation" (the default), the extra fraction of to cells with at least one from cell within r; or "count", the number of extra from cells within r of each to cell. With k, "within r" means among the cell's k nearest neighbours.

k

Cell method: use the k nearest neighbours instead of a radius.

combine

Cell method with several radii: "maxT" (max-T with the sandwich correlation across radii; up to 6 radii), "davies" (Davies' bound for the same maximum, for many radii) or "cauchy" (Cauchy combination). The max-T p-value is the multivariate normal probability of the largest |z|, computed by the quasi-Monte Carlo method of Genz and Bretz with an absolute error of about 1e-4 (by quadrature for two radii); the same inputs always give the same value.

adjustAbundance

Cell method: adjust the test for the log share of the from type in each image (default FALSE). Its effect is reported as abundance_effect. It does not separate more from cells from more densely packed ones, and it removes real effects when the share tracks the condition.

variance

Cell method: "cr2" (the default: each condition's CR2 variance, on Satterthwaite df, see Details) or "hartung_knapp" (the model-based variance, scaled by the Pearson statistic when that exceeds its df and never below CR2, on m - 2 df).

ref

Cell method: the reference level of condition.

cores

Number of threads (cell method) or cores (image method).

tableKey

Cell method with a SpatialData store or object: the name of the cell table in tables/ (by default the only table, or the one called "table").

imageInfo

Cell method: a table with one row per image, for condition, subject, covariates or a survival outcome that are not columns of the cell table: a data.frame whose imageID column, or else its row names, gives the image IDs, or the name of a table of the SpatialData store or object. Every image of the cells needs a row, and every row an image. A survival::Surv column given as condition makes a survival analysis, also from a store.

cellWeights

Optional cell weights in [0, 1], in the order of cells: a numeric vector with one weight per cell for its own cell type (for example a quality score), or a matrix (or sparse Matrix) of soft cell type membership with one row per cell and one named column per label (for example a classifier's confidence). With a matrix, from and to name its columns, and labels may overlap (a group and its subtypes). Cell method: a to cell counts with its weight, and its score is the chance that it has a from neighbour within r if each cell were a from cell with probability its from weight (allocation), or the summed from weight of its neighbours (count). The null shuffles the to weights over the cells whose from weight is below 1 (so a cell of the from type with weight 0.6 is a candidate with the remaining 0.4), and its exact mean and variance replace those of random labelling; weights of 1 give the results of the cell types. The abundance share is the from label's summed weight over the image's cells. One radius and cells in memory; pairs of a label with itself are not tested. Image method: see getPairwise().

...

Arguments of the image method: sigma, alternateResult, minLambda, weights, weightsByPair, weightFactor, weightZThreshold, window, window.length, edgeCorrect, includeZeroCells, verbose, BPPARAM. Supplying alternateResult selects the image method.

Value

A SpicyResults object. topPairs(), signifPlot(), spicyBoxPlot() and bind() work for both methods. For the cell method, $cellResults holds the full table: for the allocation effect, the pair's side ("attract" or "avoid", which sets the scale of the effect), the effect in each condition (excess_ref, excess_comp, at the average covariates), the difference (excess_difference), its standard error, df, p-value and BH-adjusted p-value, the frailty variance, the between-image variance (tau2_image) and, when the test was adjusted, what for (adjusted_for), the effect and p-value of each adjustment, and the unadjusted test (unadjusted_difference, unadjusted_p_value, unadjusted_p_adj). Every requested pair has a row: not_tested gives why a pair (or, in $radiusResults, a radius) was not tested ("one_patient_per_group", "no_information", "few_effective_units" or "no_variation"; NA when it was), and its p-value is then NA and not counted in the BH adjustment. $effect records which effect was estimated.

Details

method = "cell" (the default). In each image, the share of to cells with at least one from cell within radius r is compared with its exact expectation q if the to cells were a random choice among the cells that are not from cells. The effect (effect = "allocation", the default) is the fraction of to cells placed next to (or kept away from) from cells. For a pair that attracts (more to cells next to from cells than q over all images together) it is (observed share - q) / (1 - q): if a fraction f of the to cells were moved next to from cells, the effect is f. For a pair that avoids it is (observed share - q) / q: if a fraction f of the to cells that would have a from cell nearby were moved away, the effect is -f. Either way it does not depend on how many from cells there are or how densely they are packed. The side is chosen once per pair from all images with a condition, without the conditions, and is reported in the side column. effect = "count" gives the number of extra from cells within r of each to cell instead; it also reflects how many from cells surround a to cell (depth of infiltration), but it grows with how densely the from cells are packed, so a change in packing alone can appear as a change in co-localisation. Images are combined within patients and patients within conditions by a frailty GEE with a second random effect for the images of a patient (each image is weighted by 1 / (its sampling variance + the between-image variance), so one large image cannot outweigh the patient's other images), and the difference between conditions is tested with a CR2 cluster-robust variance on Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, with patients (subject) as the units. The difference is adjusted for any covariates, and, with adjustAbundance = TRUE, for the log share of the from type in each image; the unadjusted test is then reported alongside (unadjusted_* columns).

When nearly every cell has a from cell within r (q close to 1), there is little room for attraction and an attracting pair's images carry little information; a smaller r is more informative.

The allocation effect is bounded: an image of an avoiding pair with no to cell next to a from cell has the effect -1, and an image of an attracting pair with every to cell next to one has +1. A patient is informative at a radius when at least one of its images is not at -1 or +1. A radius where one condition has no informative patient is not tested: that condition's patients all have the same effect, so its spread is exactly 0 and the standard error would rest on the other condition alone. Its p-value is NA (with adjustment, adjusted_for is "none (no_information)"), and it is left out of the combination over radii. With more than two conditions, a pair where any condition has no informative patient is not tested.

The standard error of the difference is the sum of each condition's own CR2 variance, on Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; with adjustment, the CR2 variance of the adjusted design. variance = "hartung_knapp" keeps its own variance.

For a self-pair (from = to) every cell can carry the label, so random labelling moves both the cells counted and their neighbours. Its variance is the exact random-labelling variance of the self-pair (for the radius graph and for the k nearest neighbours), not the variance of a pair of two types.

With the allocation effect, an image whose room on the pair's side (the to cells without a from neighbour expected by chance for an attracting pair, those with one for an avoiding pair) is below one cell is not used: its effect could not show the pair's side, and could be large in the other direction. The side is chosen first, from every image.

A patient's weight within its condition grows with the information of its images, so one or two patients can carry nearly all of a condition's weight. A radius where a condition's effective patients (Kish's (sum w)^2 / sum w^2 of the patients' weights w) fall below the smaller of 3 and half the number of its patients that contribute at that radius is not tested: its p-value is NA (with adjustment, adjusted_for is "none (few_effective_units)"), and it is left out of the combination over radii. A condition of 3 patients with equal weights can therefore be tested. With more than two conditions, a pair where any condition falls below this is not tested.

Images with a missing condition are left out of every step: the choice of the side, the between-image variance and the tests.

method = "image" (the original spicyR test). A per-image L-function summary of each pair is compared between conditions with a weighted linear model, or a mixed model when subject is given (Canete et al. 2022). With cellWeights (see getPairwise()), cells enter each label with a weight, for example the confidence of a classifier, instead of through a single cell type.

Examples

data("diabetesData")
# spicyR Cell: patients ("case") are the units
# the extra fraction of Th cells, and of beta cells, with a Tc cell within 50 units
res <- spicy(diabetesData, condition = "stage", subject = "case", r = 50,
             from = "Tc", to = c("Th", "beta"))
topPairs(res)
#>                         from   to         level excess_ref excess_difference
#> Tc__Th__Onset             Tc   Th         Onset  0.3199387       0.072364141
#> Tc__Th__Long-duration     Tc   Th Long-duration  0.3199387       0.001750948
#> Tc__beta__Onset           Tc beta         Onset         NA                NA
#> Tc__beta__Long-duration   Tc beta Long-duration         NA                NA
#>                           p_value     p_adj
#> Tc__Th__Onset           0.5909207 0.5909207
#> Tc__Th__Long-duration   0.9852766 0.9852766
#> Tc__beta__Onset                NA        NA
#> Tc__beta__Long-duration        NA        NA
res$cellResults
#>                         from   to         level    side excess_ref
#> Tc__Th__Onset             Tc   Th         Onset attract  0.3199387
#> Tc__Th__Long-duration     Tc   Th Long-duration attract  0.3199387
#> Tc__beta__Onset           Tc beta         Onset    <NA>         NA
#> Tc__beta__Long-duration   Tc beta Long-duration    <NA>         NA
#>                         excess_difference         se       df   p_value
#> Tc__Th__Onset                 0.072364141 0.12597874 4.925793 0.5909207
#> Tc__Th__Long-duration         0.001750948 0.09031631 5.040000 0.9852766
#> Tc__beta__Onset                        NA         NA       NA        NA
#> Tc__beta__Long-duration                NA         NA       NA        NA
#>                             p_adj        tau2 tau2_image            not_tested
#> Tc__Th__Onset           0.5909207 0.001361901 0.05860949                  <NA>
#> Tc__Th__Long-duration   0.9852766 0.001361901 0.05860949                  <NA>
#> Tc__beta__Onset                NA          NA 0.14011289 one_patient_per_group
#> Tc__beta__Long-duration        NA          NA 0.14011289 one_patient_per_group

# the extra number of Tc cells within 50 units of each Th cell
resCount <- spicy(diabetesData, condition = "stage", subject = "case", r = 50,
                  from = "Tc", to = "Th", effect = "count")

# the original image-level test
resImage <- spicy(diabetesData, condition = "stage", subject = "case",
                  from = "Tc", to = "Th", method = "image")
#> Dropping unused levels. Using stage = Non-diabetic as base comparison group. If this is not the desired base group, please convert cells$stage into a factor and change the order of levels(cells$stage) so that the base group is at index 1.
topPairs(resImage)
#>        intercept coefficient   p.value adj.pvalue from to
#> Tc__Th  1.622672    5.961811 0.6122509  0.6122509   Tc Th
